data.name: Feeroza
data.gender_notes: Feeroza is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A shining light, bringing joy and illumination. The name Feeroza carries the meaning “Bright, shining light” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Feeroza usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, shining light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of enlightenment and inner radiance
data.etymology: Feeroza belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright, shining light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Feeroza total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

It has been embraced by various Muslim communities with pride and affection, and many Babies have been named Feeroza as a symbol of their parents' dreams and aspirations for them.

The name serves as a reminder to keep one's inner light burning brightly by practicing virtues, seeking knowledge, and striving for self-improvement. By living a life that reflects the light of the divine, one can bring joy, hope, and illumination to themselves and those around them.

historical_references.reference: Feeroza, a fifteenth century queen of Sri Lanka, was known for her beauty, grace, and wisdom. She rose to power after the death of her husband, King Parakramabahu VI, and ruled as regent for her infant son, Dharmasoka. During her reign, she maintained peace and prosperity in the kingdom and is remembered for her patronage of Buddhism and culture.

Another Feeroza, a seventeenth century Muslim queen of Bengal, gained fame for her military prowess and diplomacy. She played a significant role in the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan's conquest of Bengal and was rewarded with the title 'Rani Padmavati'. She is also known for her patronage of arts, architecture, and education.
